newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto's daughter calls for peace, unity at poll.
newsitem.headline: Suharto's daughter calls for peace, unity at poll.

text.p: President Suharto's eldest daughter called for peace and unity as she kicked off Indonesia's general election campaign for the ruling Golkar party in volatile central Java on Sunday.
"We must be watchful of security. We must be orderly," Siti Hardyanti "Tutut" Rukmana, one of seven Golkar chairmen and a prominent businesswoman, told about 10,000 people gathered on a fairground.

Populous central Java has been hit by pre-campaign disturbances in recent weeks, with violent confrontations primarily between supporters of Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP).
Golkar, the PPP and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are the only three groups legally permitted to contest the polls.
There were no reports of trouble as the April 27-May 23 campaign got underway.
Dressed in a skirt and blouse in the yellow Golkar colour, Tutut also appealed to the country's 124.7 million voters to go to the polls for the national and local elections on May 29.

"We must all join in the general election because it ensures the future of the nation. You must not join 'Golput'," she told an enthusiastic audience, referring to the practice of deliberately spoiling votes.
Golkar says it is seeking just more than 70 percent of the vote after winning 68 percent in the last elections in 1992.
Tutut told the crowd to disperse peacefully after the rally before she went on to visit Jepara, a district town known for its furniture-making about a two-hour drive from Semarang.
The rally in Semarang, an industrial port of about 750,000 people, was held in bright sunshine, with a stiff breeze whipping the yellow Golkar flags.
The wind also tore away a huge banner attached to a Ferris wheel at the edge of the fairground with the slogan "Golkar is my choice".

Organisers said they had anticipated a turnout of more than 100,000, but witnesses estimated the crowd in the development promotion fairground numbered around 10,000. Some participants said they felt they were obliged to come because they were party members.
Tutut put on a charismatic display, keeping the crowd laughing and calling up members of the audience to the platform -- where they were carefully frisked before approaching to answer questions.
Security was low-key, however, with few uniformed police in sight. Golkar officials and youth groups provided the main security.
Semarang and the surrounding countryside was a sea of Golkar yellow. For every 100 Golkar banners there appeared to be only about 10 for the United Development Party and one for the PDI.
